body: D3D12 will still need to implement the changes to `command_render_bind_vertex_buffers` and verify that `vertex_format_create` is correct.
We can now create vertex buffers, so `true` was no longer valid. Introduced specifically named APIs to create a UMA for SSBO, VBO, etc
A lot of the naming was taken from the compatibility version of `canvas.glsl`
As noted, this is only ever used by TYPE_RECT, so no sense including it when `USE_ATTRIBUTES` is defined. Should be a minor optimisation for PARTICLE, MESH and MULTI_MESH types.
Moved these to match the compatibility version

🏎️ We're taking advantage of the new `binding` field, which means we are using the same buffer binding slot for all vertex attributes. Rather than binding 8 buffers (with potentially different frequency and stride values) every draw call, we now only bind one buffer. 

A binding specifies how the buffer is read by the GPU, controlled by `frequency` and `stride`. Assuming the driver doesn't coalesce all 8 bindings, that reduces bookkeeping from 8 to 1 buffer.
We're not adding an instance to the VBO buffer, but instance_count > 0 for the batch to be committed. This is just a flag that is masked out later.
Make sure we don't accidentally try to add the other types to the batch
We can now use UMA for vertex buffers
Take advantage of the move-assignment operator to avoid reallocating.

There are many cases where the engine binds the same buffer multiple times. By tracking unique buffers, we only perform this logic once, which reduces unnecessary allocations, as `draw_trackers` is a vector, so the same buffer would be added multiple times.
I still have to tidy up this function and remove some of the unnecessary logic. It _behaves_ the same, so for performance testing it should be fine.
Switching to Span means we can avoid allocations at call sites. We should evaluate all calls and use FixedVector, as the sizes in the renderer_rd are all known at compile time.
This was incorrect.
This is worth a separate core PR. Move semantics are desirable for all our containers, and that would make this PR completely non-core.
Do these `noexcept` have any effect? We don't use exceptions and as far as I know we don't use this directive elsewhere
True – I'll remove them

@Ivorforce Are you okay with merging this change in this PR? I don't really want to block this PR while we wait for this optimization to be applied to other containers. 

My preference in general is for core optimizations to be in the same PR where they are used as well so the git history shows why certain changes were needed

Generally agree that optimizations should be introduced only when needed, but move semantics are needed for all our containers (and most of them do have it already). Looks like I just forgot to add them for hash maps.
Core changes particularly have a habit of being 'snuck in' in bigger PRs, which can make it very hard to spot and estimate the repercussions of. Generally I would expect core changes to be beneficial to not only the use-case of a PR, but the codebase in general. For example, I would normally expect benchmarks for common cases, if it's optimization related. That's why I prefer them in separate PRs when possible.

Anyway, they look fine to me (granted `noexcept` is removed), so I'm OK with merging them in here.
`noexcept` has been removed - thanks for the feedback!
